name: eval2 fixes from the owner's fifth review (MOTH-115, 117, 131, 132, 135, 141, 143, 144): the tape, Elliot's note, Singapore clothes in the wardrobe and its close-up, the bath on the tub, the trundle drawer out with the paper inside, each packed thing in its own edit.
notes: Edits keep the picture's geometry so tools/lift.py can lift each change against its base.

cases.prompt:
Style: a polished, finished illustration drawn for a game, not a picture book for toddlers; clean dark-ink outlines on everything, a shadow side on every object and soft cast shadows from one light source, so things sit solidly on their surfaces; smooth colour with gentle shading, a faint paper-grain texture and a gentle vignette at the edges. Bright and clear, not hazy or dark. The attached picture is a crop from the room this belongs to: copy only its style, hand and palette, not its objects. Draw it alone on a pure flat white background: no surface, no shadow on the ground, no frame, no border, no text, nothing else in the picture. The object fills most of the frame. No words, letters, numbers or symbols anywhere in the picture.

The object: a roll of clear sticky tape on its own, with no dispenser, lying flat on its side as it lies on a desk, seen from the front and a little above, the way a ten-year-old standing at her desk sees it: a squat ring, its top face an oval, the shiny layered band of clear tape round its outside clearly showing its thickness all along the front, the pale brown cardboard core inside it and the hole through the middle. A short loose end of tape curls off the front.
cases.note: MOTH-117: one picture for the room, the pen-pot close-up and the strip; never squashed to fake a desk

cases.prompt: The attached picture is finished and approved. Redraw it as the same picture, keeping absolutely everything exactly as it is, the same objects in the same places at the same sizes, the same colours, light and drawing style, except for this one change: the clothes inside the open wardrobe are now a ten-year-old girl's clothes for hot, sunny Singapore. On the hanging rail hang exactly seven summer clothes on wooden hangers, from left to right: (1) a sunny yellow cotton sundress with thin straps; (2) a pale pink short-sleeved blouse with a frilled collar; (3) a sky blue short-sleeved cotton T-shirt with no hood; (4) a white short-sleeved T-shirt printed with small pink hearts; (5) a lilac short-sleeved cotton dress; (6) a coral pink T-shirt with a small white star; (7) a light denim pinafore dress. The two shelves below the rail hold neat folded piles of light summer clothes: T-shirts in white, pale pink, yellow and pale blue, and cotton shorts in light denim, khaki and pink; no jumpers, no knitwear, no coats. The top shelf, the box's edge and the red ribbon stay exactly as they are. Nothing else changes anywhere. No words, letters, numbers or symbols anywhere in the picture.
cases.note: MOTH-135: the rail named thing by thing, the same words as the close-up
